title: Publish the probe-interval operator command on the shared runtime contract, human-only, and regenerate the client
description:
SPIDR child of task-078232fb9b9d4c06a5faf3c02adaf705, cut by architect-5ac70ba8 on 2026-09-07. The parent's DoD spanned three separable responsibilities and measured ~25 files against the board's 20-file cap, so the command SURFACE and the health READ were cut off the parent's durable-record core.

THIS ROW TAKES the parent's DoD 1 COMMAND HALF. The parent keeps DoD 1's durable record, store port and bounds, plus DoD 2 (scheduler honours the interval per environment) and DoD 3 (boot re-registration). dependsOn the parent because the command handler writes THROUGH the interval store port the parent lands - publishing a kind whose handler has nothing to write to is a producer with no consumer edge.

MEASURED AT HEAD by architect-5ac70ba8 (2026-09-07 ~13:20Z), so plan against this and re-measure before editing:
- The kind roster is `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:91-92` ("deployment.deploy", "deployment.migrate_down", "deployment.rollback", "deployment.set_target", ...).
- THE EPIC RAIL'S MIRROR LOCATION IS STALE. It says "two mirrors live under apps/control-room". Measured `git grep -rln GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST -- apps packages adapters tools` returns SEVEN source files and NONE under apps/control-room: apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-readiness-evidence-collector.ts, apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-readiness-evidence-producers.test.ts, apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-deploy-target-offers.ts, packages/control-room-client/generator/generate.ts, packages/control-room-client/src/contract-digest.test.ts, packages/control-room-client/src/contract-pins.ts, packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts. Re-census with the full-tree grep yourself; the relevant package is `@moe/control-room-client` (packages/control-room-client), and `@moe/control-room` (apps/control-room) is a SEPARATE package that must also be run.
- PRECEDENT ROWS on this board for exactly this shape: task-b3888068 (DONE, "The two environment kinds reach the shared runtime contract and the generated client") and task-a2409cba (DONE, "environment.set_variable and unset_variable are published operator-only"). Read their completion records before designing the fence.

NOT IN SCOPE: the durable interval record, the store port, the scheduler, boot re-registration (all the parent's), and the health read disclosure (task filed alongside this one).
definitionOfDone: The kind is added to the shared runtime roster at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts and is HUMAN-ONLY: MCP-excluded, asserted by code AND layer at the fence, following the precedent task-a2409cba set for environment.set_variable.

ALL FOUR GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors are re-censused by a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types and updated - the measured source set is listed in this row's description and must be re-measured, not trusted. The generated client is regenerated rather than hand-edited.

The command handler writes the per-environment interval THROUGH the store port landed by task-078232fb - no second write path and no direct store access. Bounds and refusals are the port's: out-of-range and unknown-environment each assert code AND layer.

Roster coverage is BIDIRECTIONAL (global rail): every advertised kind is served AND every served kind is advertised, enumerated from the dispatch seam's handled kinds and asserted as set-equality, not subset.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. The control-room legs are mandatory because the digest mirrors are invisible to `pnpm test` and to the daemon leg.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE AND BASELINE. NO EDITS. Three confirmations, and one correction that decides whether you run the control-room leg.
(a) **THE ROSTER**: `sed -n '85,100p' packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` — `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS`, ALPHABETICAL, deployment kinds at :91-92, `environment.set_variable`/`unset_variable` at :94.
(b) **THE DIGEST CENSUS, FULL TREE, ALL FILE TYPES** (DoD 2): `git grep -rln GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST -- apps packages adapters tools`. I measured SEVEN source files and NONE under `apps/control-room`: `apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-readiness-evidence-collector.ts`, `apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-readiness-evidence-producers.test.ts`, `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-deploy-target-offers.ts`, `packages/control-room-client/generator/generate.ts`, `packages/control-room-client/src/contract-digest.test.ts`, `packages/control-room-client/src/contract-pins.ts`, `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts`. Re-run it; do not trust my list. Of those seven, the two under `apps/daemon/src/cutover/` and the affordance module carry the literal but are probably not roster-sensitive — read each and say which mirrors need editing and which merely mention the constant. That is DoD 2's "re-censused", and a verdict per file is what it asks for.
(c) **THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS MOST. DO NOT SKIP THE CONTROL-ROOM LEG.** The epic rail says "two mirrors live under apps/control-room"; (b) finds none there, and this row's description calls the rail stale on that basis. **BOTH ARE HALF RIGHT, AND "NO CONTROL-ROOM WORK" IS THE WRONG CONCLUSION.** Read `git show --stat 4f6bfbf0` — task-b3888068, the landed precedent for this exact operation. It touched SIX source files and TWO are under `apps/control-room`: `src/data/data-adapter.test.ts` and `src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx`. They are ROSTER COUNT PINS, not digest mirrors, which is why the digest grep misses them — and they are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg. So the rail's CONCLUSION is right while its REASON is wrong.
(d) **THE FENCE PRECEDENT**: `sed -n '210,226p' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts`. Read the comment about `environment.set_variable` before writing yours — it states why TWO fences are wanted: "that one stops an agent reaching the kind over a transport, this one stops the wrapper minting a session to take it as staffed work. Different actors, so both are wanted."
BASELINE, quoted with `Test Files N passed` count lines, because this row spans three packages and the precedent's own commit lists `runtime-vocabulary.ts`, `generated-client.ts`, `generated-coverage.test.ts`, `runtime-contract.test.ts`, `data-adapter.test.ts` and `approve-plan.test.tsx` as CONTESTED with another row: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.

THE KIND ON THE SHARED ROSTER, AND THE CLIENT REGENERATED (DoD 1 roster half, DoD 2). Copy task-b3888068's landed shape (`git show 4f6bfbf0`).
(1) `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` — add the kind to `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS`, KEEPING THE ROSTER ALPHABETICAL. The parent row calls this a per-environment probe interval, so choose a name that sorts with the kinds it belongs to. **PICK ONE SPELLING AND RECORD IT IN THE COMPLETION SUMMARY** — task-078232fb (the store port), task-eb37494e (the dispatch and handler) and the health-read row all name this kind, and a second spelling is how a four-row chain drifts.
(2) `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts` — the contract arm the precedent updated.
(3) **REGENERATE `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts`; DO NOT HAND-EDIT IT** (DoD 2). The generator is `packages/control-room-client/generator/generate.ts` and the file is itself one of the seven digest carriers, so a hand edit desynchronises the digest from the roster it is supposed to pin and the failure surfaces far from its cause. Find and run the generate script; if you cannot, STOP AND REPORT rather than editing the generated file.
(4) `packages/control-room-client/src/contract-pins.ts` and `src/contract-digest.test.ts` carry the digest. **QUOTE THE BEFORE AND AFTER DIGEST VALUES IN YOUR RECORD**: a digest that did NOT move after a roster addition means the regeneration did not run, and that is the failure this clause exists to catch.

THE COUNT PINS THE DIGEST GREP CANNOT FIND (DoD 2, DoD 5) — the step step 1(c) exists to justify. These red only under their own package legs, and nothing else runs them.
(1) `packages/control-room-client/src/generated-coverage.test.ts` — the generated-surface coverage pin the precedent updated.
(2) `apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts` — a roster count pin; the precedent's diff shows a one-line change here.
(3) `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx` — the same shape.
FOR EACH, READ WHAT IT ACTUALLY PINS BEFORE CHANGING A NUMBER: if it is a bare total, say so and update it; if it enumerates kinds, ADD the kind rather than incrementing a count. A count pin bumped without reading what it counts is how a roster gains a member nothing serves.
Run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` after this step and quote their count lines. Do not leave a red here for step 5 to discover — these two legs are the whole reason DoD 5 names them.

THE HUMAN-ONLY FENCE (DoD 1 second half) — **TWO ROSTERS, AND BOTH ARE WANTED**. It lands in THIS row, with the advertisement, deliberately: a kind advertised on the shared roster before its fence exists is reachable by an agent for however long the next row takes.
(1) `apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.ts` — the MCP EXCLUSION. Stops an agent REACHING the kind over a transport.
(2) `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts` — the SPAWN fence, beside `environment.set_variable`/`unset_variable` at :220 and `project.set_agent_provider` at :223. Stops the WRAPPER minting a session to take it as staffed work.
WRITE THE REASON AT THE SITE, in the register the neighbours use — each of them says what the kind would let an agent do. Here: how often production is probed is an operator's judgement about monitoring cost and noise, and an agent able to widen the interval could quietly silence the surface that reports an outage.
ARMS, in the roster tests that already enumerate these fences BY EXACT LIST — add the kind, never loosen the assertion: `apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts` (:231 enumerates the deployment kinds), `apps/daemon/src/mcp-main.test.ts` (:227, same list), `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` (:355, the human-approver roster).
**ASSERT THE FENCE REFUSAL BY CODE AND LAYER**, not merely that the call did not succeed (DoD 1, global rail 1). Two fences can both refuse; the arm must say which one did, or it stays green when the wrong one starts answering first.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. Load `adversarial-self-review` and read your own diff as an attacker first.
DRILLS — `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths FIRST and record the output. This row creates NO new file, so every path is TRACKED and an empty `git diff -- <path>` in a call SEPARATE from the restore is valid proof; state that no untracked path was mutated, so global rail 13 is answered rather than ignored.
THREE DRILLS, each quoted with its failing line:
(i) **THE FENCE DRILL** (DoD 1): remove the kind from `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts` and confirm the exclusion arm reds ON THE CODE AND THE LAYER. Then restore it and remove it from `agent-spawn-contract.ts` instead, and confirm a **DIFFERENT** arm reds. If one arm covers both removals, one of the two fences is untested and the "different actors" reasoning is asserted nowhere — strengthen it rather than reporting a pass.
(ii) **THE HAND-EDIT DRILL** (DoD 2): hand-edit the generated client instead of regenerating, and confirm the digest pin arm reds. This proves the pin actually guards the generator rather than being copied along with it.
(iii) **THE COUNT-PIN DRILL** (DoD 2, step 3): revert ONE of the two `apps/control-room` count pins and confirm `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` reds while `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck` stay green. That is the measurement behind step 1(c), and it is the evidence that the control-room leg was mandatory rather than precautionary.
GATES — standalone and foreground, ONE command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line, because an exit-0 leg with NO count line ran nothing and a bad `--filter` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 (global rail 8): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. A bare root `pnpm test` covers no `apps/**` file; say that rather than quoting it. Attribute any red outside this row's thirteen files against your step 1 baseline — six of them are CONTESTED with another row in the precedent's own commit — and disclose foreign red verbatim rather than owning it or calling it green.
SELF-REVIEW AND RECORD, in completionSummary plus one row comment for detail over the cap: the EXACT kind spelling, so task-078232fb, task-eb37494e and the health-read row all use the same one; the before-and-after contract digest values, proving the regeneration ran; the full re-censused mirror list from step 1(b) WITH A VERDICT PER FILE (edited, or mentions the constant only); which of the two `apps/control-room` count pins moved and what each actually pins; the three drill outcomes with their failing lines; and that DoD 3 and DoD 4 are delivered by task-eb37494e47924b659a0a1a77060b36eb, which dependsOn this row and task-078232fb — this row deliberately advertises and FENCES the kind, and the dispatch registration that serves it lands there. Named verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 13 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 20 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
**I SUBMITTED THIS ROW'S FULL SCOPE FIRST AND THE DAEMON HARD-REJECTED IT AT 22 DISTINCT FILES (cap 20).** So it is split, and the split is along the seam the board itself used before: task-b3888068 (DONE) landed the environment kinds on the shared roster and the generated client; task-a2409cba (DONE) published them operator-only. The new sibling is task-eb37494e47924b659a0a1a77060b36eb, PLANNING, dependsOn [this row, task-078232fb].

**THE CUT IS NOT WHERE I FIRST WANTED IT, AND THE REASON MATTERS.** My first instinct was surface-then-handler: roster plus client here, fence plus dispatch plus handler there. I rejected it. A kind advertised on the shared runtime roster with no fence is reachable by an agent for as long as the second row takes to land, and "advertise now, fence later" is a security ordering, not a paperwork one. **SO THE FENCE LANDS WITH THE ADVERTISEMENT** — both rosters, both arms, in this row — and the DISPATCH REGISTRATION plus the HANDLER go to the sibling. That also puts the dependency where it belongs: the handler needs task-078232fb's store port, and this row needs nothing from it, so this row is ungated and can land immediately while the port row is still in planning.

DoD 3 and DoD 4 therefore move to task-eb37494e with their own DoD text. This row keeps DoD 1 (roster AND fence), DoD 2 and DoD 5. Step 5 makes the worker state that partition in the completion record so QA does not read two clauses as silently dropped.

**THE CORRECTION I MOST WANT CARRIED FORWARD**, because the epic rail and this row's own description are each half right and the wrong conclusion is one grep away: the rail says "two mirrors live under apps/control-room"; the full-tree digest grep finds NONE there, which is what the description flags as stale. But `git show --stat 4f6bfbf0` — the landed precedent for this exact operation — touched two `apps/control-room` files: `src/data/data-adapter.test.ts` and `src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx`. They are ROSTER COUNT PINS, not digest mirrors, so the grep cannot see them, and nothing but `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` runs them. **The rail's conclusion is right; its reason is wrong.** A worker who trusted "the rail is stale" and skipped that leg would ship two red files. Step 1(c) states it, step 3 does it, and drill (iii) proves it by reverting one pin and showing only the control-room leg reds.

REJECTED — merging steps to fit under the cap. The rejection message forbids it explicitly and it would not have helped: the cap counts files, not steps.

planningNotes.risks:
1. **DO NOT CONCLUDE "NO CONTROL-ROOM WORK" FROM THE DIGEST GREP.** Two `apps/control-room` roster COUNT PINS break on a roster addition, are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg, and only `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` runs them. This is the single easiest way to ship this row red, and drill (iii) is written to prove the leg was necessary.
2. **REGENERATE THE CLIENT, NEVER HAND-EDIT IT** (DoD 2). `generated-client.ts` is itself a digest carrier; a hand edit desynchronises the digest from the roster it pins. **A digest that did not MOVE after a roster addition means the regeneration did not run** — quote before and after, or the clause is unevidenced.
3. **TWO FENCES, TWO ARMS.** If removing the kind from either roster reds the SAME arm, one fence is untested. Drill (i) removes each separately and requires DIFFERENT arms to red.
4. **ASSERT CODE AND LAYER ON THE FENCE REFUSAL.** Both fences can refuse; an arm that checks only a code cannot tell which one answered and stays green when the wrong one starts answering first (global rail 1).
5. **ONE SPELLING FOR THE KIND, ACROSS FOUR ROWS.** task-078232fb (store port), task-eb37494e (dispatch and handler) and the health-read row all name it. Record the exact string in the completion summary; a second spelling is how a chain like this drifts.
6. **DoD 3 AND DoD 4 ARE NOT DROPPED, THEY MOVED** to task-eb37494e47924b659a0a1a77060b36eb. Say so in the completion record or a reader will score this row against clauses it no longer owns.
7. **DO NOT TOUCH THE DISPATCH REGISTRATION OR THE HANDLER** from this row — `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts`, `daemon-command-payload-keys.ts`, `daemon-command-registry.ts` and their arms belong to task-eb37494e, which will edit them in a shared worktree.
8. **SIX OF THIS ROW'S THIRTEEN FILES WERE CONTESTED** in the precedent's own commit. Baseline both legs in step 1 and attribute foreign red rather than owning it.
9. The kind is advertised here and SERVED by the sibling. Between the two landing, a dispatch of the kind refuses as unknown — that is the correct, fenced, fail-closed state, and it is why the fence lands here rather than there.
